clue.text: Man's name for sacred flower

parts.note: a flower is something that flows, a river, abbreviated R on maps
Coleridge's Kubla Khan names Alph as the sacred river, so sacred points to that river's name

explanation.surface: Someone explains what a particular man is called in honour of a holy bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' is crossword code for a river (it flows), giving R; the 'sacred' flower is Alph, the sacred river of Coleridge's poem Kubla Khan. Together they make a boy's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Ralph is a common masculine forename, so it is a man's name.

clue.text: Mocks policeman I set up in administrations

indicators.note: the policeman and I go inside the word for administrations

parts.note: rules are periods of government or administration

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means the letters are turned to read upwards

parts.note: CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, British detectives

explanation.surface: A detective sneers at the governments after setting himself up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set up' turns CID + I into IDIC, which goes 'in' RULES after the R.
explanation.definitionFit: To ridicule is to make fun of, so mocks.

clue.text: Primate raised spirits with, article in Spanish

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means the whole run of letters is read from the bottom up

parts.note: rum is a spirit, used here as a mass noun
el is the Spanish word for the

explanation.surface: Someone lifted their drinks alongside a Spanish newspaper piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns RUM + EL upwards, giving LE + MUR.
explanation.definitionFit: A lemur is a tree-dwelling primate of Madagascar.

clue.text: Help bear in acrobatic act

parts.note: to give a hand is to help
to stand something is to bear it

explanation.surface: A helper supports a performer doing a gymnastic trick.
explanation.definitionFit: Balancing upside down on one's palms is a classic gymnastic feat.

clue.text: Achievement of winner or person who's next

parts.note: what a winner achieves is success
taken as written

explanation.surface: A champion's triumph, or the one who comes after them in line.
explanation.definitionFit: A successor is the one who follows on, the next holder of a post or title.

clue.text: Viciously attacked poet died

parts.note: Richard Savage was an eighteenth-century English poet, friend of Samuel Johnson

explanation.surface: A poet was brutally attacked and killed.
explanation.definitionFit: Savaged means mauled or attacked fiercely.

clue.text: According to Kipling, Judy O'Grady's brother-in-law?

definitions.text: According to Kipling, Judy O'Grady's brother-in-law?

parts.words: According to Kipling, Judy O'Grady's brother-in-law?
parts.note: Kipling's line says a certain officer's lady and Judy O'Grady are sisters under their skins, so that officer would be Judy's brother-in-law

explanation.walkthrough: Kipling's poem 'The Ladies' ends: 'For the Colonel's Lady an' Judy O'Grady / Are sisters under their skins!'
explanation.definitionFit: If the officer's wife and Judy are sisters, the army officer married to the wife is Judy's brother-in-law.

clue.text: Support for board to relieve pressure on pound

parts.note: to ease is to relieve pressure or strain
L stands for the pound, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: A board member's plan to lift the strain on sterling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'board' suggests a company board or currency board; it is a painter's board or blackboard.
explanation.definitionFit: An easel is a frame that holds up a painting board or blackboard.

clue.text: Vessel, or its centre when enlarged

definitions.meaning: a vessel is a ship or boat
the middle of the word vessel is SS, the abbreviation which, written out in full, names a powered ship

explanation.walkthrough: The centre of 'Vessel' is SS, the prefix on ships' names; 'enlarged' means the abbreviation written out in full.
explanation.definitionFit: A steamship is a vessel driven by steam, and SS, the middle of the word vessel, is its abbreviation.

clue.text: The thinking man's sculptor

parts.note: reads as the sculptor intellectuals favour, but means the artist who made the famous statue of a man thinking

explanation.walkthrough: 'The thinking man's X' is a phrase for an intellectual's choice; here it is the maker of the bronze statue The Thinker.
explanation.definitionFit: Auguste Rodin sculpted The Thinker, a seated man deep in thought.

clue.text: Not even a bit original, this book?

parts.note: a dime is ten US cents, less than a bit, the old 12.5-cent unit, so it is not even a bit
novel means new or original

explanation.surface: A critic sneers that a book has not the slightest originality.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'bit' in American money is 12.5 cents (two bits make a quarter), so a ten-cent dime is not even a bit.
explanation.definitionFit: A dime novel was a cheap sensational paperback sold in America, a kind of book.

clue.text: Further success for expedition

definitions.meaning: to ... is to prosper or help succeed, as in 'God ...'
expedition in its old sense is promptness or haste

explanation.definitionFit: Speed once meant prosperity, as in wishing someone good speed, and it also means quickness, which is what expedition means in its sense of haste.

clue.text: Divine female heard but not seen in programmes

indicators.note: the word for programmes is only heard, not written, so a sound-alike is wanted

parts.note: a run of broadcast programmes is a series

explanation.surface: A goddess is audible but invisible on television shows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heard but not seen in' signals that the word for programmes is spoken, not spelt: SERIES sounds like the name of the Roman goddess of grain.
explanation.definitionFit: Ceres was the Roman goddess of agriculture, so a divine female.

clue.text: Runners for old cricket side

parts.note: the amateurs who played against the professional Players in the old annual cricket fixture, and the word also names those who might run errands for a side

explanation.walkthrough: From 1806 to 1962 English cricket held a Gentlemen v Players match, amateurs against professionals.
explanation.definitionFit: The amateur team in the historic Gentlemen v Players cricket fixture bore this name.

clue.text: Northern area map concealed by youth

indicators.note: the word for a map is hidden away inside the word for a youth

parts.note: a lad is a youth
a plan is a map or diagram

explanation.surface: A boy has hidden a chart of the far north.
explanation.definitionFit: Lapland is a region in the far north of Scandinavia and Finland.

clue.text: Formal sign for elections

parts.note: prim means stiffly proper or formal
Aries is a sign of the zodiac

explanation.surface: An official notice is put up announcing polling day.
explanation.definitionFit: Primaries are preliminary votes held to choose party candidates.

clue.text: Broke up? Had to be remoulded with glue

indicators.note: remoulding shapes the letters again, so the following words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Something that broke had to be repaired by moulding it again with glue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be remoulded' rearranges HAD and GLUE ('with' joins them). 'Broke up' looks like breakage, but it means collapsed with laughter.
explanation.definitionFit: To break up is an idiom for collapsing into fits of mirth.

clue.text: Alliance to raise standards in combination

parts.note: a union is an alliance
to jack up is to raise, as with a car jack

explanation.surface: A coalition promises to improve standards by working together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'standards' suggests levels of quality; they are flags. The British flag combines the crosses of England, Scotland and Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: The British national flag merges three national crosses, flags joined into one.

clue.text: Little known competitor Godolphin, perhaps

definitions.meaning: an obscure contender whose chances are unknown
the Godolphin Arabian, a dark bay stallion of the 1700s, is an example of a literally dark steed

explanation.definitionFit: An outsider of unknown form is called this in racing and politics, and the Godolphin Arabian, a dark-coated founding stallion, literally was one.

clue.text: Auster operating from place in Wiltshire

parts.note: Auster is the Latin name for the south wind, so S plus WIND
on means working or operating, as a machine is on

explanation.surface: An Auster aircraft flies from an airfield in the county of Wiltshire.
explanation.walkthrough: Auster sounds like a light aircraft maker, but it is the classical south wind: S (south) + WIND. Wiltshire is an English county; Swindon is its largest town.
explanation.definitionFit: Swindon is a large town in the English county of Wiltshire.

clue.text: Arresting Pole in a bad way

parts.note: N is the north pole
ailing means unwell, in a bad way

explanation.surface: A Polish man in poor health is being arrested.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole' looks like a Polish man; it is a pole of the earth, N for north.
explanation.definitionFit: Nailing someone is slang for catching or arresting them.

clue.text: Mule playfully hunted

definitions.meaning: a mule is a backless shoe worn indoors
in the party game hunt the ___, a shoe is passed round secretly and searched for

explanation.definitionFit: A mule is a backless indoor shoe, and the children's party game 'hunt the ___' has players searching for one such shoe.

clue.text: This poet listeners might take for philosopher

indicators.note: people hearing the name would confuse it with a word that sounds the same

parts.note: Herbert Spencer was a Victorian philosopher

explanation.surface: An audience might mistake this poet for a thinker.
explanation.walkthrough: Edmund Spenser, poet of The Faerie Queene, and Herbert Spencer, the philosopher, have names that sound identical.
explanation.definitionFit: Edmund Spenser was the Elizabethan poet of The Faerie Queene.

clue.text: Steadiest characters tossing across the Atlantic

indicators.note: the letters of the word are thrown about into a new order

explanation.surface: The steadiest people are being thrown about on an ocean crossing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'characters tossing' means the letters of STEADIEST are tossed into a new order.
explanation.definitionFit: Stateside means in or towards the USA, seen from Britain across the ocean.

clue.text: Thackeray's character not natural cheat

definitions.meaning: Becky, the scheming heroine of Vanity Fair
in music a note raised a semitone is not natural

explanation.definitionFit: Becky Sharp is Thackeray's antiheroine in Vanity Fair; in music a raised note is the opposite of natural; and a sharper is a swindler.

clue.text: Golfer's feat excelled by Ancient Mariner?

definitions.text: Golfer's feat excelled by Ancient Mariner?

parts.words: Golfer's feat excelled by Ancient Mariner?
parts.note: a golf score of two under par is bettered by three under, named after the seabird shot in Coleridge's poem

explanation.walkthrough: In golf an albatross (three under par) beats this score (two under); Coleridge's Ancient Mariner shot an albatross.
explanation.definitionFit: Two strokes under par on a hole is named after a large bird of prey, and the albatross score beats it.

clue.text: Any MP has maiden appearance therein

indicators.note: the answer makes an appearance within the run of words just given

explanation.surface: A Member of Parliament gives a first speech in the House.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maiden appearance' looks like an MP's first speech, but 'maiden' is the definition and 'appearance therein' tells you the answer shows up inside ANY MP HAS.
explanation.definitionFit: A nymph is a young maiden, especially a nature spirit of myth.

clue.text: Transport system covered by foreign capital

definitions.text: Transport system covered by foreign capital

parts.words: Transport system covered by foreign capital
parts.note: reads like a project paid for by overseas investment, but means the underground railway that serves Paris and other capitals

explanation.walkthrough: 'foreign capital' suggests overseas money; it is a capital city abroad such as Paris, whose underground railway carries this name.
explanation.definitionFit: The Paris underground railway is called the Métro, a system covering that capital.

clue.text: One section of the House is daunting

definitions.meaning: a house can have several wings, and this is one of them

explanation.definitionFit: Read as two words it is one wing of a building; as one word it is the present participle of awe, filling with dread, which is daunting.

clue.text: Transient, liable to change immediately

indicators.note: the letters of the preceding word are apt to be altered into another order

explanation.surface: Something fleeting may shift at a moment's notice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'liable to change' rearranges the letters of TRANSIENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Instanter is a formal or legal word for at once, without delay.

clue.text: Coach may move this weak team member

definitions.meaning: a coach is a bus that carries travellers
a team member who does not pull their weight is said to be carried

explanation.definitionFit: A coach carries riders who pay a fare, and a team carries a member who contributes little.

clue.text: A couple of sovereigns somebody got for foreign money

parts.note: K for king and R for rex or regina, two monarchs' abbreviations
one means a person or somebody

explanation.surface: Two gold coins and someone else's cash were traded for currency abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sovereigns' suggests gold coins, but here they are monarchs: K (king) and R (rex). 'got for' simply joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The krone is the currency of Denmark and Norway.
